about: The quick start's steps, in order: the one source for docs/quick-start.md's table (render-quickstart.py) and for status.sh. Each step is at most one command or one visit to a page, plus the check that says it is done. check.type is config (fleet.env exists with OWNER, PLAN and CLAUDE_PLAN), verify (verify.sh --only <groups> passes), files (each file is on that repo's default branch, so its starter pull request is merged) or ask (status.sh --mark <id> once you say it is done; an ask check with "record": "content" is also done once add-content.sh has recorded your choices). link is a kit-relative path to the docs section that explains the step. An optional step is listed but never blocks the next. track is base (guidance, skills, settings, hooks, machines: what /adopt sets up) or evals (what exists only for the eval loop: what /adopt-evals adds); status.sh --track limits its report to one. A step that serves both is base, and its run text says which part only evals use. A verify check runs with its step's track (verify.sh --track): a base step never looks at skills-evals or what serves only it, and an evals step looks only at those, so the base needs no skills-evals and adding evals never undoes a base step. A verify check with "by_hand": true (the App installations) also takes status.sh --mark <id>: gh's own sign-in cannot read GET user/installations (HTTP 403), so verify.sh then accepts your answer for that step instead and says so.

steps.title: Write fleet.env
steps.run: `cp bootstrap/fleet.env.example fleet.env`, fill in `OWNER`, `OWNER_TWO`, `PLAN`, `CLAUDE_PLAN` and `TIME_ZONE`

steps.title: Choose optional skills, guidance and git hooks
steps.run: `bootstrap/add-content.sh --items recommended --dry-run`, then the same without `--dry-run` (or name the items you want, or `--items none`)

steps.title: Create the five base repos
steps.run: `bootstrap/create-repos.sh` (all but `skills-evals`, which only evals use: the evals track creates it)

steps.title: Store the privacy denylist
steps.run: `bootstrap/set-secrets.sh --only privacy --denylist <file outside every repo>`

steps.title: Copy repo-settings and merge it
steps.run: `bootstrap/copy-starter.sh starter/repo-settings <you>/repo-settings`, then review and merge the pull request

steps.title: Create the environments
steps.run: `bootstrap/create-environments.sh` (its `routine-fire` environment waits for the evals track's `skills-evals`)

steps.title: Create the three base GitHub Apps
steps.run: `bootstrap/create-apps.sh guidance-sync settings-admin settings-read` (GitHub's App manifest flow, once per App, in the browser)

steps.title: Install the base Apps
steps.run: Open each `https://github.com/apps/<slug>/installations/new` link `create-apps.sh` printed and pick the repos it names

steps.title: Copy the App id into repo-settings
steps.run: `bootstrap/create-environments.sh` again

steps.title: Drop the example repos from fleet.yml
steps.run: In a pull request on `<you>/repo-settings`, remove the three `example-site-*` entries from `repo-settings/fleet.yml` (unless you have those repos); the tests read that file, so none needs changing

steps.title: Copy _agent-guidance and merge it
steps.run: `bootstrap/copy-starter.sh starter/agent-guidance <you>/_agent-guidance`, then review and merge

steps.title: Drop the example repos from repos.yml
steps.run: In a pull request on `<you>/_agent-guidance`, remove the `example-site-*` names from `repos.yml` `cron_coverage.fleet` and `skills_bootstrap.repos` (unless you have those repos)

steps.title: Copy the two registries and merge them
steps.run: `bootstrap/copy-starter.sh starter/agent-skills <you>/acsi-agentskills` and `bootstrap/copy-starter.sh starter/agent-skills-private <you>/acsi-agentskills-private`, then review and merge

steps.title: Copy wsl-automation and merge it
steps.run: `bootstrap/copy-starter.sh starter/wsl-automation <you>/wsl-automation`, then review and merge

steps.title: Pin every skills.lock to your registry
steps.run: `bootstrap/regenerate.sh skills-locks`, merge, then run it again for the other four repos

steps.title: Pin the skills-bootstrap hook
steps.run: `bootstrap/regenerate.sh hook-pin`, then merge

steps.title: Pin the scheduled-run-health reusable
steps.run: `bootstrap/regenerate.sh run-health-sha`, then merge the three pull requests

steps.title: Pin the Codex Cloud bootstrap
steps.run: `bootstrap/regenerate.sh codex-pin`, then merge

steps.title: Regenerate the action lockfiles
steps.run: `gh extension install github/gh-actions-lock`, then `bootstrap/regenerate.sh actions-lock` and merge what it opens

steps.title: Apply fleet.yml: protect every repo
steps.run: `bootstrap/apply-settings.sh` (and `--owner <OWNER_TWO>` signed in as that account; `fleet.yml` declares no `skills-evals` until the evals track adds it)

steps.title: Set up each durable machine
steps.run: On each one: `bootstrap/install-machine.sh` (add `--with-codex` if you use Codex)

steps.title: Schedule the machine jobs
steps.run: First, in the distro (or on Linux or macOS), copy your wsl-automation clone's `config/settings.env.example` to `~/.config/wsl-automation/settings.env` (every job reads it) and check its repositories, `LESSONS_CLONE` and `WSL_AUTOMATION_AGENT_OWNER_ROOTS` (the folder that holds your clones). It ships `SKILLS_EVALS_URL=none` and `WAITING_FEED_URL=none`: the session miner and the usage census run code from skills-evals, and the waiting feed pushes to a feed repository the base does not create, so on the base they log that they skipped and exit 0 (step 42 turns the first two on; set `WAITING_FEED_URL` when you create `waiting-feed`). Windows: `./scripts/register-tasks.ps1` in an elevated PowerShell 7, in your wsl-automation clone; on the base the jobs that do work are the ccstatusline config sync, the WSL memory log, the Docker watchdog and memory curation, and the optional waiting feed skips each minute until you create `waiting-feed` and set `WAITING_FEED_URL`. Linux or macOS: nothing to schedule on the base (`scripts/unix/install-schedule.sh` schedules only the usage census and the session miner, which serve evals, and the optional waiting feed), so mark this step done, or run `bash scripts/unix/install-schedule.sh <systemd|launchd|cron> --jobs waiting-feed` if you use the waiting feed

steps.title: Set up your cloud environments
steps.run: At https://claude.ai/code, give each cloud environment the setup script from acsi-agentskills' `docs/multi-repo-delivery.md` and the network allowlist from _agent-guidance's `docs/reference/network-allowlist-claude-environments.txt`

steps.title: Create the fleet worker routine
steps.run: At https://claude.ai/code/routines, one task (the Fleet worker, maintenance role): an API trigger only (no schedule), the GitHub connector, its prompt in docs/routines.md; set FLEET_WORKER_FIRE_URL and FLEET_WORKER_FIRE_BEARER on _agent-guidance, whose fleet-worker-fire.yml fires it (create-environments.sh left the URL `none`, which skips the fire with a "not set up yet" notice; set it to the routine's fire URL. This step's check is that the URL is no longer `none` and the bearer is set; the token is shown once, and bootstrap/README.md has the commands). Pick the model its table in docs/routines.md names (Sonnet on Pro) instead of leaving the selector on Default, which follows the account default (Opus on Pro, by Anthropic's model page); remove the connectors it does not need. The Loop worker serves the eval loop, so the evals track creates it (step 41)

steps.title: Create the prompt-audit sweep routine
steps.run: At https://claude.ai/code/routines: API trigger only; store its fire URL and bearer on _agent-guidance as PROMPT_AUDIT_SWEEP_FIRE_URL (variable) and PROMPT_AUDIT_SWEEP_FIRE_BEARER (secret); the token is shown once, and bootstrap/README.md has the commands. Pick the model its table in docs/routines.md names (Sonnet on Pro) instead of leaving the selector on Default, which follows the account default (Opus on Pro, by Anthropic's model page); remove the connectors it does not need

steps.title: Create the agent changelog watcher routine
steps.run: At https://claude.ai/code/routines: daily at 01:03 UTC (on Pro, weekly: `3 1 * * 1`), in an environment of its own with no variables. Pick the model its table in docs/routines.md names (Sonnet on Pro) instead of leaving the selector on Default, which follows the account default (Opus on Pro, by Anthropic's model page); remove the connectors it does not need

steps.title: Schedule memory curation
steps.run: A weekly task from a claude.ai project thread, and the same on each durable machine (docs/routines.md has both prompts). Set the project's Threads model to Sonnet (Project settings > General > Threads): the task runs as threads in that project, and a new project runs Opus. If your account has no Projects yet (a public beta, rolling out gradually), the machine task alone covers it, and the step is done

steps.title: Create skills-evals
steps.run: `bootstrap/create-repos.sh skills-evals` (with its labels and its `persistent/eval-results` branch), then `bootstrap/set-secrets.sh --only privacy --denylist <the same file as step 3>` again: it stores `PRIVACY_DENYLIST` in `skills-evals`, whose required `test` job fails closed without it, and leaves the base repos' copies alone

steps.title: Copy skills-evals and merge it
steps.run: `bootstrap/copy-starter.sh starter/skills-evals <you>/skills-evals`, then review and merge

steps.title: Turn on the session miner and the usage census
steps.run: On each durable machine, in `~/.config/wsl-automation/settings.env`, change `SKILLS_EVALS_URL=none` to `SKILLS_EVALS_URL=https://github.com/<you>/skills-evals.git`; then, in your wsl-automation clone, run `bash scripts/run-session-miner.sh --dry-run` once (a scheduled miner run refuses until one dry run has succeeded). Windows: the tasks are already registered. Linux or macOS: `bash scripts/unix/install-schedule.sh <systemd|launchd|cron> --jobs usage-census,session-miner`

steps.title: Create the three eval GitHub Apps
steps.run: `bootstrap/create-apps.sh eval-improve roster registry-read` (GitHub's App manifest flow, once per App, in the browser)

steps.title: Install the eval Apps
steps.run: Open the `https://github.com/apps/<slug>/installations/new` link `create-apps.sh` printed for each and pick the repos it names; then add `skills-evals` to the installations of `guidance-sync`, `settings-admin` and `settings-read`

steps.title: Create the Loop worker routine
steps.run: At https://claude.ai/code/routines, one task (the Loop worker, loop role): an API trigger only (no schedule), the GitHub connector, its prompt in docs/routines.md; set LOOP_WORKER_FIRE_URL (replacing the `none` create-environments.sh wrote) and LOOP_WORKER_FIRE_BEARER on _agent-guidance (create-environments.sh already set LOOP_WORKER_EVERY_HOURS from CLAUDE_PLAN). fleet-worker-fire.yml skips its fire while EVALS_REPO is none and fires it once the next step flips EVALS_REPO to skills-evals, so this comes first. Pick the model its table in docs/routines.md names (Sonnet on Pro) instead of leaving the selector on Default, which follows the account default (Opus on Pro, by Anthropic's model page); remove the connectors it does not need

steps.title: Create its environment and copy the roster App's id
steps.run: `bootstrap/create-environments.sh` again (the `routine-fire` environment in `skills-evals`, `ROSTER_WRITER_APP_ID` in `repo-settings`, and `EVALS_REPO` on `_agent-guidance`, which flips from `none` to `<owner>/skills-evals`)

steps.title: Pin skills-evals' generated files
steps.run: `bootstrap/regenerate.sh run-health-sha` and `bootstrap/regenerate.sh actions-lock` again, then merge what they open in `skills-evals`

steps.title: Declare skills-evals in fleet.yml and the coverage list
steps.run: `bootstrap/regenerate.sh evals-fleet`, then merge the pull requests it opens: in `repo-settings` it moves `skills-evals`' element from `repo-settings/fleet.evals.yml` into `repo-settings/fleet.yml`, and in `_agent-guidance` it adds `skills-evals` to `repos.yml` `cron_coverage.fleet`

steps.title: Apply fleet.yml to skills-evals
steps.run: `bootstrap/apply-settings.sh` again: it now includes `skills-evals`

steps.title: Decide eval.yml's default fixture
steps.run: `.github/workflows/eval.yml`'s `fixture` default, `evals/workflow-path-audit/required-check-routing`, ships with the kit and runs as it is: keep it, or change it to a fixture of your own in a pull request on `<you>/skills-evals`

steps.title: Create the eval runner routine
steps.run: At https://claude.ai/code/routines: an API-triggered routine with the prompt in skills-evals' `docs/routine/eval-runner-prompt.md`; keep the bearer it shows once and its `trig_...` id for the next step. Pick the model its table in docs/routines.md names (Sonnet on Pro) instead of leaving the selector on Default, which follows the account default (Opus on Pro, by Anthropic's model page); remove the connectors it does not need

steps.title: Store the eval runner's bearer and trigger id
steps.run: `bootstrap/set-secrets.sh --only routine-fire`

steps.title: Optional: let eval.yml trade OIDC for an Anthropic token
steps.run: In the Anthropic Console, set up workload identity federation for `skills-evals`, put its four ids in fleet.env, then `bootstrap/create-environments.sh`

steps.title: Optional: the dashboard and the explorer page
steps.run: Create two claude.ai artifacts: the private build as a Dashboard artifact (skills-evals' `dashboard/README.md`, Adopting it), refreshed every 2 hours, and the public build `explorer/dist/artifact/index.html` as an artifact with your `latest.json` beside it; both start private
